GetTagVal.summary: Retrieves the tag values for a specified tag key from reported traces.

GetTrace.summary: You can invoke the GetTrace API to obtain trace details.

schema.description:
The trace ID, which is the unique identifier of the trace.

You can obtain the trace ID on the **Trace Explorer** page in the Managed Service for OpenTelemetry console or by calling the [SearchTraces](~~2399674~~~) operation.

The type of the application. You can leave this parameter empty or set the value to `XTRACE`. We recommend that you leave it empty.

*   Empty value: queries traces reported from Managed Service for Prometheus and Application Real-Time Monitoring Service (ARMS).
*   `XTRACE`: queries only traces reported from Managed Service for Prometheus.
The ID of the region.
The page number.
The number of entries on each page. Maximum value: 100.

HaveStack.description:
Indicates whether the span has child spans. Valid values:

*   `true`
*   `false`

ServiceIp.description: The IP address of the server on which the span resides.

ParentSpanId.description: The ID of the parent span.

Duration.description: The duration of the span. Unit: milliseconds.

RpcId.description: The parent-child and sibling relationship between spans. For example, span 1.1 is the parent of span 1.1.1, and span 1.1.2 and span 1.1.1 are siblings.

Timestamp.description: The timestamp when the span was generated. Unit: microseconds.

TraceID.description: The trace ID, which is the unique identifier of the trace.

Key.description: The tag key of the span.

Value.description: The tag value of the span.

items.description: The log events in the trace.

Timestamp.description: The timestamp when the log event was generated. Unit: microseconds.

items.description: The tags in the log event.

Key.description: The tag key of the log event.

Value.description: The tag value of the log event.

ListIpOrHosts.summary: Queries IP addresses or hostnames in trace data. You can obtain all IP addresses of an application or in a region.

schema.description: The ID of the region.

The type of the application. You can leave this parameter empty or set this parameter to `XTRACE`. We recommend that you leave this parameter empty.

*   If you leave this parameter empty, applications monitored by Managed Service for OpenTelemetry or Application Real-Time Monitoring Service (ARMS) can be queried.
*   If you set this parameter to `XTRACE`, only applications monitored by Managed Service for OpenTelemetry can be queried.

schema.description:
The time interval at which you want to query metric data. Unit: milliseconds. Minimum value: 60000. 

> If you set this parameter to 2147483647, all data in the specified time interval is returned.

The beginning of the time range to query. The value is a timestamp that is accurate to milliseconds.

>  The value of this parameter is of the LONG type. Precision loss may occur during serialization or deserialization. The value must be less than or equal to 9007199254740991.

The end of the time range to query. The value is a timestamp that is accurate to milliseconds.

>  The value of this parameter is of the LONG type. Precision loss may occur during serialization or deserialization. The value must be less than or equal to 9007199254740991.
The field based on which you want to sort the returned entries.
The maximum number of entries that you want to return.

The name of the metric. Valid values:

- `appstat.incall`: trace statistics 
- `appstat.sql`: SQL statistics

The order in which you want to sort the returned entries. Valid values:

- ASC: ascending order 
- DESC: descending order
The ID of the proxy user.
The filter conditions.

Key.description: The key of the field that you want to use to filter the returned entries.

Value.description: The value of the field that you want to use to filter the returned entries.

schema.description: The dimensions of the metric that you want to query.

items.description: The dimensions of the metric that you want to query.

schema.description: The measures of the metric that you want to query.

items.description:
If you set the **Metric** parameter to `appstat.incall`, the **Measures** parameter has the following valid values:

- `rt`: response time 
- `count`: total number of records that you want to return 
- `error`: number of errors 
- `exception`: exception 
- `errorrate`: error rate 
- `qps`: number of requests per second 

If you set the **Metric** parameter to` appstat.sql`, the **Measures** parameter has the following valid values:

- `rt`: response time 
- `count`: total number of records that you want to return 
- `error`: number of errors 
- `slowcount`: number of slow calls

SearchTraces.summary: Call the SearchTraces operation to query a list of traces. You can filter traces by time, application name, IP address, span name, tag, and other criteria.

- `XTRACE`: Query only XTRACE traces.

- `false`: Ascending order.

List of tags.
